d: The HIV pol enzyme that copies the viral RNA genome into DNA. It does not proofread, so it introduces the mutations that drive drug resistance; NRTIs and NNRTIs both target it.

The herpes simplex and varicella-zoster enzyme that adds the first phosphate to acyclovir. Because only infected cells make it, the drug is activated where the virus replicates; losing it causes resistance.
An empty shell that self-assembles from the HPV L1 capsid protein. It looks like the virus to the immune system but carries no DNA, so the vaccine made from it cannot cause infection.
A mononucleosis-like illness 2 to 4 weeks after HIV infection, with fever, rash, pharyngitis and lymphadenopathy, when viral load is very high but antibody tests may still be negative.
